catalog_quote: In Yine, primary stress is uncontroversially assigned to the prosodic word from right-to-left, regularly falling on the penultimate syllable ... This also appears to be the default tendency in the list of Mashco Piro data in Table 1. Of 24 individual words, 14 exhibit penultimate primary stress. However, one half of these 14 examples (viz., 7) contain only two syllables. ... In these longer words, antepenultimate stress outnumbers penultimate stress by 9 tokens to 7. However, this is complicated by two potentially confounding factors. First, two of the forms with antepenultimate stress have a long vowel in that position ... Second, four of these forms end with the apparent suffix /-řa/ ... all three of the words containing four syllables or more have penultimate stress ... audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all fragments of the deciding quotation and the exception quote are verbatim in the publisher text we hold of Parker 2015b at sec. 5.2.4, pp. 16-17, and the conclusion remark is on p. 18 as the locator says. (2) Deciding source: a 2015 phonology sketch by the only linguist ever to transcribe the language, explicitly refusing to adopt a stress rule on a 24-word corpus; 'undetermined' is exactly what the source says. The companion data paper Parker 2015a (downloaded to independently confirms: stress falls within the last three syllables, long vowels attract it, no reliable generalization possible. sources.quote: 'With respect to the placement of (primary) stress, it appears to always be located on one of the last three syllables of the word. However, this is complicated by the fact that in many of the utterances there is probably more than one morpheme involved, and possibly even two distinct words. ... a couple of longer words do appear to exhibit secondary stress. sources.note: Only post-2015 work Glottolog ties to the languoid; an ethnographic thesis drawing on post-2014 contact via Yine interpreters that might report new Mashco Piro utterances or intelligibility remarks. Unlikely to state a stress rule, but it is the one place a larger word sample could surface; would at most refine, not change, 'undetermined'.
